cards.title: Introduction to Migrations
cards.content:
As your Flask application evolves, your database schema needs to change too. Database migrations allow you to safely manage these structural changes over time without losing data.

Instead of manually altering tables in SQLite or PostgreSQL, we use migration tools to track and apply these changes programmatically.

cards.title: Flask-Migrate and Alembic
cards.content:
In the Flask ecosystem, database migrations are handled by Flask-Migrate, which is a wrapper around Alembic (a database migration tool for SQLAlchemy).

pip install Flask-Migrate

It integrates seamlessly with Flask-SQLAlchemy to automatically generate migration scripts based on your model definitions.

options.text: Flask-Migrate is a wrapper around Alembic.
Flask-Migrate relies directly on raw SQL scripts only.

cards.title: Initializing the Migration Repository
cards.content:
To start using migrations in your Flask app, you need to initialize the extension and create a migration repository.

from flask import Flask
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from flask_migrate import Migrate

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'

db = SQLAlchemy(app)
migrate = Migrate(app, db)

This adds the db CLI commands to your Flask application.

cards.title: CLI Initialization Command
cards.content: To initialize the migration folder structure in your project directory, you run the command: flask db [blank] .

content.instructions: Order the standard workflow steps for applying a schema change in Flask-Migrate.

items.text: Modify or create your SQLAlchemy models in Python code.
Run 'flask db migrate -m "description"' to generate the migration script.
Review the generated Alembic migration script in the migrations folder.
Run 'flask db upgrade' to apply the changes to the database.

cards.title: Anatomy of a Migration Script
cards.content:
A generated Alembic migration script contains two main functions: upgrade() and downgrade().

def upgrade():
    # Operations to apply the change
    op.add_column('user', sa.Column('twitter_handle', sa.String(length=80)))

def downgrade():
    # Operations to reverse the change
    op.drop_column('user', 'twitter_handle')

Always inspect these scripts before running upgrade, especially when doing auto-generation.

options.text: It can automatically detect every single table rename and column rename accurately.
It detects table structure changes like new columns, but complex changes like renames often require manual script adjustments.
It connects to production databases directly to guess changes.
It completely eliminates the need for the upgrade command.

cards.title: Migrations in Production
cards.content:
When deploying your Flask application to production, running migrations safely is critical.

  • Never run flask db migrate in production; generate scripts locally and commit them to version control.
  • Run flask db upgrade as part of your CI/CD deployment pipeline before starting the new app server.
  • Always take a database backup before upgrading production databases.

cards.title: Applying Migrations in Production
cards.content: To apply pending database migrations on your production server, you execute the terminal command: flask db [blank] .

cards.title: Summary
cards.content:
You have learned how to manage database schemas using Flask-Migrate and Alembic.

Key takeaways:

  • Use init once, migrate for new changes, and upgrade to apply them.
  • Always review auto-generated Alembic scripts.
  • Keep migration history in version control.
